tickets.subject: Clarification on Info Needed to Start NPI Process
tickets.description: Hi team, I’m prepping to kick off a new product intro and want to make sure I’m not missing anything before I reach out to the GTM folks. Is there a checklist or specific info I need to provide when I communicate the launch? I remember something about needing to explain what we’re launching and who it’s for, but not sure if there’s more to it. Do I need to include financials or timing details at this stage? Thanks!

comments.body: Hi Sara, great question! There’s actually a section in the GTM Enablement motion policy that outlines what you need to cover when you start the NPI process. You’ll want to include what the launch is (features, services, etc.), why we’re launching (the value prop and any financial justification you have), who the target market is, and any timing considerations. Also, make sure the product is far enough along and that GTM teams have bandwidth. Let me know if you need the link to the doc!

tickets.subject: Which YouTube channel should I upload my demo video to?
tickets.description: Hey team, I just finished recording a demo for a new feature we're rolling out. It's pretty polished and I think it could be useful for both customers and maybe even for some internal folks. I'm not sure if this should go on the main GitLab YouTube channel or the Unfiltered one. Is there a guideline for which channel is best for this kind of content?

comments.body: Hi Sara! Great question. Generally, if your demo is polished and aimed at customers or the broader community, it should go on the Branded channel. If it's more casual or meant for internal or community members, Unfiltered is the way to go. Also, anything on the Branded channel needs to go through digital production for a quick quality check. Let me know if you need help connecting with them!

tickets.subject: Clarification on Sending Security Release Notification Email
tickets.description: Hi team, I need to send out a security release notification to our customers next week. I saw there are different templates for operational emails, but I'm not sure if I should use the general non-demand gen template or if there's a specific one for security releases. Also, do I need to submit the issue even if I don't have the final copy ready yet? And who handles pulling the recipient list for this type of send? Thanks!

comments.body: Hi Mei! For security release notifications, there’s a dedicated issue template you should use (not the general one). You can go ahead and open the issue as soon as you know you’ll need the send, even if you’re still working on the final assets. As for the recipient list, you’ll need to open a separate list request issue—Marketing Ops doesn’t handle the list pull. Let me know if you need the links or have any other questions!

tickets.subject: Clarification on CSM Team Stamping for Opportunities
tickets.description: Hey team, I noticed that sometimes the [Comp] CSM Team field on Opportunities gets auto-filled, but I'm not totally sure when that's supposed to happen. Is it only when the CSM Team is 'Scale', or does it depend on the order type too? I just want to make sure I'm not missing anything when creating or closing Opps. Thanks!

comments.body: Hi Sara, great question! The CSM Team gets stamped onto the Opportunity if the CSM Team for the Customer Success Manager is 'Scale', or if the Order Type is one of a few specific ones (like New - Connected, Growth, Contraction, and both Churn types). Let me know if you need the full list or more details on how it works.

tickets.subject: Zendesk Tickets Not Showing Up in Gainsight
tickets.description: Hi team, I noticed that some Zendesk tickets aren’t appearing in the company view in Gainsight. Is there something I need to do to make sure all tickets are syncing properly? Also, is there a way to check if the Zendesk Organization IDs are matched up with our Salesforce accounts? Thanks!

comments.body: Hi Mei, thanks for flagging this. The sync between Zendesk and Gainsight relies on the Zendesk Organization ID being present in Salesforce. If some tickets aren’t showing, it might be because the Org IDs aren’t up to date in Salesforce. You can try re-importing the Zendesk Org IDs into Salesforce to help with the matching. Let me know if you need the steps for that or if you’re still seeing issues after trying this.

tickets.subject: Clarification on Content Review Timeline for Customer Program Materials
tickets.description: Hi team, I’m working on some new onboarding materials for our customer success program and wanted to check what the process is for getting this content reviewed. Is there a specific timeline I should plan for, and do I need to get approval from anyone outside our Digital Customer Programs group? Just want to make sure I’m following the right steps before I start drafting.

comments.body: Hi Mei, thanks for reaching out! Yes, any new content or adaptations from other GitLab sources need to go through a review process outside of our team. The review checks for accuracy, style, and readability. You should expect it to take about 10 business days, so roughly one milestone. Let me know if you need help with the initial scoping or finding existing materials to reference.

tickets.subject: Question about managing multiple events in Accelevents
tickets.description: Hi team, I’m working on setting up a couple of events in Accelevents and I was wondering if it’s okay to have more than one event open in different tabs at the same time? I need to compare some settings between them and it would be a lot faster if I could just switch between tabs. Is there any issue with doing this, or is there a recommended way to handle it?

comments.body: Hi Sara, thanks for reaching out! Actually, we recommend not having multiple events open in the same browser at once. It can cause some weird issues with the settings getting mixed up between events. If you need to compare, it’s best to use different browsers or incognito windows for each event. Let me know if you need more details or help with this!
